title: 200 years after the first dinosaur, scientists use brain scans on a 100-million-year-old snake fossil from Brazil
summary: The Times of India Science Desk reports that researchers have applied brain-scanning techniques to a 100-million-year-old snake fossil from Brazil. Using modern imaging, scientists aim to study the fossilized braincase to learn more about ancient reptile anatomy and evolutionary links to other prehistoric species.

## Recent Research

Researchers have used brain-scanning techniques on a 100-million-year-old snake fossil from Brazil, aiming to image the fossilized braincase and related internal structures. The work, reported by the Times of India Science Desk, seeks to shed light on prehistoric reptile anatomy and evolutionary relationships, using non-destructive imaging to access details otherwise hidden inside rare fossil specimens.

- Subject: 100-million-year-old snake fossil from Brazil
- Method: Brain-scanning and non-destructive imaging of the braincase and internal structures
- Goal: Reveal details of prehistoric reptile anatomy and clarify evolutionary relationships
- Reported by: The Times of India Science Desk
